text:
Disclaimer: I have been coming to Clancys for the better part of at least 12 years.  Back in college I was here every Thursday.  I've developed a good relationship with the wait staff and management.  Clancys was always a cross between a dive and a pub.  That is what I liked about it.  There was nothing stuffy or pretentious about it.

Anyway, I heard they were renovating the place and was curious to check it out once they were done.  I went with my best friend (who has been coming as long as I have) and my girlfriend who has gone twice before they renovated.  The most noticeable change right away is the outside is a different color than the off white color it used to be.  We get inside and we are floored at the changes: faux hardwood, granite counter top tables, fancy bar backsplash, nothing on the walls, a fireplace/lounge area...we were stunned.  We only had to wait about 5-10 min for a table, but that was because the hostess never came and got us.  The manager was the first to notice how long we were waiting and got us to a table (manager also checked up on our table which is always appreciated).  The menus are not placemats anymore, but actual real menus.  The previous menu is largely intact, which some noticeable changes (pizza and flatbreads? really?).  We order the calamari for the table and was as delicious as we remember.  My girlfriend had the crab corn chowder, which was great.  The gf got the boneless wings in the original sauce.  I had some of hers and they were still pretty good (the wings were always phenomenal before, so that is good).  My friend ordered something different from the menu, chicken and broccoli alfredo pasta.  He said it was good, but a little too heavy on the alfredo sauce.

I decided to try a new menu item instead of just falling back on my old crutches.  I ordered the mac and short rib sandwich on texas toast.  When it arrived I knew I shouldn't have been shocked.  It was on nice crispy texas toast, but it was almost completely mac and cheese with tiny bits of beef short rib.  So I basically ate a mac and cheese sandwich because I was starving.  Thankfully the gf didn't eat all of her wings.  Tip: Do not order this sandwich....ever.

The servers at Clancys are no longer only women (nothing against male servers, but females in general, especially at Clancys were some of the most friendly and accommodating).  We got a gentleman server who was undoubtedly the most unfriendly and inattentive I have ever experienced at Clancys.  We had to ask for refills (no-no #1) and looked about as happy as a turkey on Thanksgiving.  He never offered a dessert menu (the gf wanted dessert) and didn't realize there was one until we saw another table receive their dessert.  We didn't bother ordering and went to Creanies in Sicklerville afterwards (see that review!).

Overall, I don't like what they have become.  The menu is the same as it was before (mainly pub food), but the place looks like an upscale Italian restaurant.  It looks like they didn't want to alienate the regulars by changing the menu, but wanted to attract an entirely new crowd with the decor.  I for one am incredibly disappointed.  This would have easily been 5 stars a few months ago.  I just can't do it now.  I don't know what prompted this change (new ownership?), but I honestly don't see myself going back which makes me sad.  The place used to pride itself as being that casual and fun neighborhood pub.  If I were ever to go back, I would try and spot an old server to wait on us because the one we got was horrible.

Also, there is no longer fresh popped popcorn for the tables.  Another great thing now gone for....whatever reason.
It's my second time here since I do not live in Reno, but if I did, I'm sure I'd be a regular . The gyros are super yummy! The location is cute and the staff are friendly.
2 weeks ago they delivered to my location but today they say they can't and it's less than 3 miles away. Seems strange. The food is just ok and customer service obviously stinks.

I know most of the raving reviews are based on in-dining experience. But I really did not expect takeout to be this disappointing considering Covid has most of us ordering out. 

We ordered the Funghi pizza, the strozzapreti (chicken pasta) and the short rib radiatori. 

The good: the funghi pizza was really tasty and warm. It smelled irresistible. So this I recommend it. 
The pasta is fresh and served el dante. The texture of the pastas were really good. 

The bad: The takeout portion sizes of the pastas are ridiculously small. Granted it is fresh pasta, but if two steps up you are going to get twice the portion size that too for pasta, you at least need to pack solid flavors for the competitive price. 

The chicken in the pasta was dry. The strozzapreti was not salted. And, the sauce was barely there. The bowl was cold and just bland. 

Similar issues with the radiotori. Although well-salted, there was barely any sauce, which tasted no different to the chicken one (apparently in addition to parmesan cream there was supposed to be horseradish). The beef cubes were tender but lacked any flavor that married it to the pasta. So dry- and I am someone who can eat good pasta with just olive oil, salt and pepper. 

Surely with all the high praises, I want to think we got exceptionally unlucky tonight. After all the great reviews from some trusted yelpers, this experience was just shockingly bad. The disappointment is two folds because I was really looking forward to a good meal for a personal celebration. 

Not to mention, the meal took ten minutes longer than the stated pick-up time, except for the pizza, the pastas were cold. 

Until we are headed to an age of dining in again, I am not getting takeout from North Italia.

My boyfriend and I were eager to try Pure Tacos, since we live in the neighborhood and love mexican food. We went here on the first day and they have a few kinks to work out.

The value is not the best. For two orders of tacos and 2 drinks, the total came to $22. (one order consists of 2 medium-sized tacos of your choice and a small handful of chips for $8.50, after tax)

Although the tacos come with chips, I wish they were accompanied with salsa. After I ate the 2 tacos, I was a bit confused about what to do with the chips. They seemed like an afterthought. If the chips came with a small side of salsa, their presence would have made more sense.

Half of the tacos on the menu are made with quick things that were on a steam table. The other half of the tacos on the menu are made with ingredients cooked to order on a stove. Since our order consisted of 1 quick taco and 3 tacos with stove-cooked ingredients, the chicken taco was made as we ordered it, and we waited awkwardly at the register for about 5 minutes, until the tacos with stove-cooked ingredients were prepared. 

There was some ordering confusion also. After we placed our order, we were asked twice to verify (and subsequently repeat correctly) the order. There seemed to be a lack of communication between the person taking orders (who was also the cashier) and the chef. I'm sure this can be easily ironed out.

The "quick chicken taco" (which was made 5 minutes before the other tacos)  was cold by the time we sat down to eat, and it was not very flavorful. The steak taco was delicious and the steak was juicy and cooked perfectly with good flavor. The 2 fish tacos we ordered were good, but not great. It would be nice to know what kind of fish they used.

Also, since the only option for drinks is to buy them in a plastic bottle, I was puzzled by the lack of recycling containers. Many of the Gluten-free, health conscious crowd seem to be progressives who are interested in recycling, and a recycling bin would be a good addition.

Pure Tacos has tremendous potential, but I'm in no rush to return. Granted, this is their first day. They need to make ordering a quicker process and figure out an accompaniment for the chips.

Overall suggestions:
- Self-serve salsa bar (for the chips that accompany the tacos)
- Recycling for the plastic bottles
- Table-side delivery for eat-in customers who order tacos with ingredients cooked on the stove
- specify type of fish in fish tacos

text:
So I went to Mr. Martino's after a suggestion from a friend who typically has epic taste in restaurants.  As an Italian American maybe I have high standards when it comes to italian restaurants.  But this place was really a piece of work...

We called for a 6 PM reservation (my cousin was visiting with her 3 year old) and the girl on the found sounded frazzled by this.  This to her, was her busiest time of night (6PM on a Saturday) and she didn't think she could squeeze us till after 9.  She took my number in case someone cancelled.  5 minutes later the phone rang and magically a table arrived.  I figured this place was gonna be slammed from the sounds of it.

We show up to this joint and the place smells like moth balls in my grandmas attic.  Is this the quaint quirk they were talking about?  Nevermind the smell, but the fact that there was one table of two people there.  My reservation for 4 was clearly going to throw this place into bedlam.  

The waitress I'm convinced was dropped of by the short bus as everything seemed to take 2 minutes for her to process.  She really irked me.

The menu was pretty limited.  A few different pastas with the same sauces.   Nevermind that the waitress had no clue if it was going to be penne or rigatoni or linguini.  She was certainly special.

The Baked ricotta appetizer with asparagus was for the birds.  2 aspargus spears and the ricotta was bitter and soaked in oil.  Gross!

I had the spinach lasagna which was just ok, not terrible.  My aunt had the cavatelli with zucchini and basil.  It was more like zucchini surprise.  
The sad thing is we all left this place with stomach aches. UGH!

This place was a huge disappointment and for 80 bucks for 3 people who left with pains I was seriously bummed.  You can keep this place, I am NEVER GOING BACK!!  what a joke...

Third time was not the charm! After tonight's experience i may never come back again.

My previous two visits were fine. I enjoyed the atmosphere. Drinks were mediocre and not cheap but that's what you pay for the atmosphere.
Tonight it took 15 minutes after we sat down before someone came up to take our drink orders. The music was way too loud. We had to shout across the table all night. I also dont understand why you need a Dj to play top 40 crap but i'll let that slide. We were playing w the three candles on our table when someone came up and took away two of them without a word, literally right outside of our hands...um ok? And he didn't put them anywhere else either so that was just odd and a bit rude actually.

It took another 15 minutes to get our checks after we flagged down the waiter. Low and behold there was a $1 charge for "rocks". WTF? The bf had ordered two jack and cokes on the rocks which showed up in regular mixed drink glasses and did not taste like it had more alcohol than the drink we had next door. Do I give a rat's ass abt a dollar? No. But I find the practice inappropriate. I am not unfamiliar w this surcharge but I have never encountered this in St Louis. Most restaurants price their mixed drinks to include the so-called extra alcohol because it just makes more sense, especially from a customer experience perspective. I mean, how many people out there order jack and coke w out it being on the rocks to justify the double Price levels/measurements?? Just tell me how much a jack and coke is. Don't nickel and penny me on that additional 2 ounces I supposedly got by ordering it on the rocks. It's really lame.

Congratulations for swindle that dollar out of me! You just lost a champion for your business.

Pho is one of those great dishes I've discovered in recent years that hits the spot when it's cold.  Simply Pho and Grill is located in a plaza on the corner of Fletcher and Dale Mabry. It is between Core Life and the Hibachi place.

I went at night and while the restaurant is a bit small, it has a sleek look. The coolest thing is the colored rectangular panels  on the walls/aisles. It makes it look like a nightclub or a Riddler deathtrap from the Arkham video games. 

My server was nice. I decided to get seafood pho since that's something Ive never had before.  I got my food in a few minutes with the usual accoutrements of sliced fresh jalapeno, mint, and sprouts.
The only nitpick is that they don't have regular forks at the table. They have a soup spoon and chopsticks. When I use chopsticks, it's like I have the proficiency of a stroke patient. I simply use the soup spoon for broth and fork for the solid matter. 

My pho was served hot with lots of big shrimp, scallops, and imitation krab along with the usual vermicelli noodles in broth. I thought the broth was good and the serving was roughly the same as places like Saigon Deli or Pho Quyen. Since it was seafood, the cost was $11 for a regular. Regular beef was around around $9. The broth isn't quite as good as Saigon deli, but better than Quyen. I'd give it a 8/10.

The only negative was that my server pretty much left once I got my food and I couldn't get a refill of my soda or my fork until I batted my eyes at another server. Thankfully I got those and another brought my bill with due haste.

Overall: A solid place to get pho and it's nicely designed so you can bring a date too!

Friendly staff working in an awkwardly tight space. The entrance brings you through an area that allows you to look directly into the kitchen it seems like you're coming through the back door of someone's home. That's all good we were greeted promptly and seed it at the front of the restaurant where we can look out onto the Main Street. Our server Siobhan was very nice that's of our orders quickly. The food was only OK they could use some work on presentation and recipes.

The pancakes were grainy as if they were made from corn meal, the flavor was not good at all! As for the French toast it was made from standard white bread. The order was small, the bread was thinand lacking flavor, I didn't taste any vanilla, cinnamon, egg, nothing! Maybe their Irish breakfast items are better.

Biggest regret inviting guests here. Between the rudest server ever known to humankind....to forgotten food, hourlong waits for wrong food, vomiting of the bad food, clogged toilets, no accountability, insencere apologies.... to forgotten drinks...I would have walked out of this disaster without paying if they didn't already have my card at the bar. I'll spare you the details of the waitress who would ask us if we needed anything and then as we went to answer would jet away and then jet back by and say "sorry did you guys need anything?" only to pass again without stopping! The weirdest, rudest experience and the only time in my life I have never tipped. 

My brother puked up his food, my husband had a black bean burger fitting in softness for the geriatric ward, etc. etc. etc. I was up all night wishing I could have thrown up everything I consumed. 

The whole place seemed off that night and none of the staff seemed experienced with handling volume. Not that it's a big space or that I haven't seen servers handle way more. I think they're just used to having a mostly dead turnout because it sucks. This particular night every one of the ten or so tables in the place were occupied and they like couldn't handle it. It was beyond ridiculous and I'll never go back here again. We brought people to dinner here and I've never been so embarrassed.

After having tried their Zern's Farmers Market location and been impressed with not only the food but the prices, I wanted to go to this location as the menu is more extensive.  Our daughter went one day and told me that the food was good and the people who work there were very friendly.  So, during our most recent visit, I told her that we needed to have a meal there.

The restaurant works better for take out than it does for dining in as there are only about 5 booths in the place.  Once our daughter tried this location, she has been there a few more times.   This is a real mom and pop place with the husband and wife doing all the cooking.  

Before going to order our food, our daughter told me that she let the husband know that she was going to bring me along.   Not only are the folks here very friendly but they get to know their regular customers.  So, by now they knew our daughter and knew that she was 1/4  Puerto Rican.

When we got there on a Thursday night, the husband was the only one working.  He was preparing the food and taking orders.  There was one customer ahead of us.  He acknowledged us while he was preparing the other  customer's order.  When it was our turn, we gave him our order.   We ordered 4 rice with red beans, 1 yellow rice with gandules (pigeon peas), 1 order of sweet plantains, 1 order of fried plantains and 3 pastelillos with meat and cheese.  He let our daughter know that he was just about out of the yellow rice but offered to sell us a 1/2 portion at reduced cost and we agreed.

The rice and bean dishes are prepared in advance and kept in warming trays.  All the other items are cooked to order.   When it was time to ring us up,  the total cost was $34.  Since our daughter had me give part of the order, I gave it using the correct names---platanos maduros and tostones .  I bring this up because many of the menu items are translated into English which I found somewhat confusing.  For example, he calls "arroz con gandules" yellow rice with beans---which isn't exactly accurate.  Pastellilos are listed as "patties".  There are "sweet plantains" instead of platanos maduros and fried plantains instead of "tostones".  While most of their customers are Puerto Ricans, he does count among his regular customers some non-Puerto Ricans.  So, perhaps, it's best that the items are listed mainly in English.

As for the food --- Our son-in-law had the yellow rice and beans as he had tried it before and really liked it.   My husband, daughter and I had the red rice and beans, while the kids shared an order of red rice and beans and each had a pastelillo with meat and cheese.  The rice and beans not only smelled good but it was tasty.  I was surprised to see that, in addition to calabaza (West Indian pumpkin) he put some cubed potatoes in it.  The flavorings were spot on.  My only complaint was that it was on the dry side but that didn't stop me from eating it all!

My husband liked the sweet plantains so much that he pretty much ate them all, only giving the rest of us a little bit.  The fried plantains were the best I've ever had.  Many restaurants serve them overcooked, dried out and tasteless.  Here, they are sliced thinner and topped with small bits of chopped garlic.  They weren't dried out and the garlic added some nice flavoring.

The kids liked the pastelillos and 2 of them liked the rice and beans.  The youngest one suddenly decided that he didn't like it.  I wanted to say to him, "What kind of 1/8 Puerto Rican are you that you don't like rice and beans?" --- but, not to worry, I kept quiet!  I was pleased to see that the kids liked the fried plantains as well as the sweet ones.

From now on, every time we visit our daughter, if times permits, I'm going to tell her that we have to have at least one meal from here!  With good food and friendly welcoming people, well...what's not to like?

text: Love everything and almost tried everything. Ordered the sampler $13  & pork chop meal $9.  Expect to get way more than what you pay for!! The boxed were filled to the top & more than anything the good was really really good.  The oxtails omg life I wish I had just a box of those.  Whomever cooks the oxtails I LOVE YOU! It's that's serious.  Was in Sarasota & just drove by.  Worth the stop & will drive all the way to st Pete if needed.  Recommend and will return without a doubt!

So Shere-E-Punjab may be a staple for Swarthmore students venturing out for more exciting fare than Renato's and Cheng Hing's, and the food is pretty decent, but as previous reviews have intimated, they have some serious service issues. When they started offering delivery, my friends and I rejoiced - finally, decent food that didn't require a car for pickup! We ordered $40+ worth of different dishes, including several orders of naan (their naan is admittedly v. good, if overpriced). That was only the beginning of our adventure.

Well over an hour later, we called, desperate, plaintive, begging for our food. They assured us that no, they had not forgotten, and yes, it would be coming. When? we asked. Soon, they replied. We could extract no further details. It was a full thirty minutes more before the delivery guy finally limped onto campus (understand that the restaurant is a ten minute drive away, fifteen max). After bestowing a generous tip on the good man who finally alleviated our starvation, we headed inside for a feast. 

We soon discovered that we had only received one order of naan, but been charged for everything we ordered. I don't know about the rest of you, but I pretty much hate eating Indian food if I can't scoop my food with bread. We called the restaurant, and they said they were sorry, all of their people had left and they could not come bring us the naan we were missing, but they would write down our names and info, and the next time we ordered they would give us the bread we paid for for free and a discount on the meal to repay us for the trouble.

Well, maybe I'm an idiot for not getting something in writing, but I think you can guess what happened the next time I called and asked for my already-paid-for naan and discount. Not only did they not make good on the deal, they were nothing short of rude in responding to the suggestion that anyone at their establishment might ever have made such a promise.

Now, their eggplant is amazing, their mango lassies are good and their chickpeas are extremely tasty in all forms. But they are unquestionably overpriced and poorly organized. I, for one, am not going back for a repeat performance.

It's amazing how the best barbeque always seems to come from these little roadside stands, and Ice Cream's Delicious Turkey Legs and BBQ is one of the rockstars in Tampa for cranking out some incredibly wonderful smoked meats.

Drop south on 22nd Street, just 2 blocks south of Hillsborough Avenue and watch for the little red trailer tucked under the trees. You'll be able to smell the smoke as you approach, and no doubt you'll see a line of people waiting for their chance to order some damn good barbeque.

The menu is very simple......ribs, thin ends, barbequed chicken, and smoked turkey legs. The sides are baked beans, potato salad and sweet potato pie. On Thursdays and Friday's he also makes collard greens and Mac & Cheese. He'll wrap everything up in foil if you want to take it to go, or you can sit on the picnic bench under the trees and eat it right there. If you choose to sit outside on the picnic bench watch out for the ants and the flies -- in fact I'd suggest a good spray-down with Off so you don't get bitten by the fire ants.

Ice Cream is the nickname of the cook, owner, and guy in the truck, sort of a jack of all trades who really knows how to smoke the meat and produce some homemade sauce that has a nice kick. Very personable guy who is proud of what comes out of his smoker -- and rightly so. This is some incredibly tasty barbeque.

The meat is flavorful, but not dried out. The ribs were still juicy, and fall-off-the-bone delicious. My girlfriend ordered the smoked chicken, and she was in heaven. I liked everything so much that I ordered a smoked turkey leg to have for dinner later tonight. Ice Cream wrapped the turkey leg in several sheets of aluminum foil and gave me some extra barbeque sauce. When it's time for dinner, I'll just cut the meat off the bone, add the sauce, and re-heat.

The food is stellar, and you're in for a real treat when you eat here!

I don't like writing bad reviews. I'm writing this one because I don't want someone else getting sucked in by the overall high star rating. Don't. Do. It.

I landed in New Orleans late in the afternoon. After a long day of travel, I needed something before heading off to a party for the night. Consulting my Yelp app, I noticed a German restaurant steps from my hotel. Jagerhaus had great reviews, and I love German food. What could go wrong? 

I walked in after viewing the menu outside. When I opened the menu I was handed inside, it was not the same. OK. The décor is very simple. It had an informal, deli type of feel that didn't fit with the menu prices.

I am a sucker for pretzels, so I ordered one along with a bowl of the soup of the day. I had wanted the bier cheese soup I had seen on the other menu, but chicken vegetable sounded fine. I also ordered a champagne cocktail which turned out to be champagne & cranberry juice. No strawberry garnish as advertised. Things happen.

There were only a few other people seated in the restaurant, so you would expect the soup to come out quickly. Nope. As I waited, people were coming in to order the various iced coffee drinks advertised. You would expect to see a coffee bar with an espresso machine, yes? Nope. They use powdered mixes, with instant coffee, the flavorings and cream mixed together in an envelope. The bartender just emptied the foil packets (from a drawer below the counter) into a blender with ice, turned it on, and poured them in cups to go. Calling themselves a full service coffee shop is quite a stretch. Moving on. 

About 20 minutes into the wait I saw them take a pretzel from the freezer and put it in the oven. Interesting. Still no soup. Most of what I saw happening from my bar stool were the cooks reheating various foods in the kitchen. That's acceptable in some cases. Not much, if anything I saw was made to order other than a couple of things coming from the deep fryer. 

Finally about 30 minutes from when I ordered (I had checked in, so I was watching the time), the pretzel and soup arrived. I have posted pictures of both. I guess I had expected a larger bowl of soup, and I certainly expected it to come out much more quickly than it did. The flavor wasn't bad, it was pretty good actually. The pretzel, well, look at the picture. It was a Super Pretzel. You know, the ones that you see at ball games that taste like paste? They charged around $5 for the nasty thing! It was horrible, but I ate a small part of it and asked for the check. 

I don't expect food to be authentic, but I do expect it to be good. This was neither. Do yourself a favor and go to Killer Poboys or Deja Vu on the same block. You aren't missing anything here.

Edit: I went back and gave 2 stars instead of my original 1. I didn't get spat at, or see anything creepy running around, but damn it! Is it that hard to at least buy pretzels from a local baker rather than use frozen Super Pretzels? At least ACT like you're trying to serve home made food. I think I made enough other points to warrant 1 star, but I was feeling guilty actually doing it.

Love this place! I will start with that it would be five stars, but I have countless service mishaps (slow, mistakes, etc.) EVERY TIME I go. However, the food is so good that I always come back- Which should say something! Definitely try the chocolate banana marshmallow milkshake- in which you can add a shot of rum for $4- and my favorite, the New City Jack burger. I didn't include a picture because I ate it so quickly  Nothing better than a burger with chorizo sausage!

Got the Red Kale Salad: and two of the ingredients were Broccoli and Zucchini. There was 1 piece of broccoli and 0 Zucchini.   The portion for $15 was NOT close to being worth $15.

I went back and mentioned there was there was 1 piece of broccoli and 0 zucchini.... their answer "yea, it can kinda be hit or miss" !!!  really? 'Hit or Miss'?!   LOL

I will NEVER waste my money there again.

My brunch buddy and I came here for the first time after our morning run at Forest Park, and I am glad we came here! We got lucky and beat the big brunching time on Saturday. I am a huge fan of David Bailey's restaurants, so I had high expectations during my first visit here. The moment I walked into the restaurant, I knew I would instantly love this place. The interior had that downtown, urban-feel but the space felt inviting. The staff were friendly, and we were greeted by a smiley-faced hostess. 

I would have to say the menu was a bit overwhelming which is a problem for me because I can be very indecisive. Especially at a time when I came back from a morning run. Everything sounded so good on the menu! My eyes were all over the place! Oh no! What if I get the wrong dish that doesn't satisfy my crepe cravings? That's why you always bring a buddy to share each other's plates. 

We got the smoke sirloin #4 ($10.95) with red onion, arugula, goat cheese, & tomato jam and the Marinated Spicy Chicken #2 ($8.95) with fontina & baby arugula. We really enjoyed the chicken crepe and could care less about the smoke sirloin. The crepe was made with perfection, and every bite seem to taste better and better. I would recommend bringing visitors here for brunch if you're hanging around downtown to explore the Arch and City Museum (City Museum is a MUST!). 

Don't worry, Rooster. I'll be back for more! :0)
Fabulous gyro with lots of meat on a fresh pita -- great hummus and tzatziki sauce too!  Definitely my favorite "downtown lunch" place.

I'm not gonna lie- when I heard that Master P was opening a burger place, I had my doubts. I thought it was all a gimmick, so I had to head over and check it out for myself.

After much anticipation, I headed to Big Poppa's for lunch. I was on a mission to discover if the burgers here were indeed, "Bout It Bout It". Walking in, I immediately loved the vibe of the place; it's like an old diner with a modern feel and I was given a friendly greeting by the smiling staff. The combination of counter and table service here is like many burger joints. You order your food at the counter, the staff gives you a number brings your order right to your table.

I thought I knew for sure what I was getting, but then, I saw it: They have a fried chicken sandwich! Of course they have a fried chicken sandwich. Why wouldn't they?

The thought crossed my mind, "Do I dare? Do I order a burger AND a fried chicken sandwich? I can't come to a burger place and not get a burger, but chicken sandwiches are hot right now. Should I get both?" My heart answered, "Absolutely!" and my stomach agreed, so I got the fried chicken sandwich meal, which came with fries and a drink, and I got a Big Poppa Bacon Burger as a nice little side. Hey, this is all for research purposes.

I first looked at the chicken sandwich and saw two big fried chicken breasts dressed to the nines with tasty fries on the side. Truth be told, the fries here are more like potato wedges, but that's no complaint. I bit into the massive sandwich and I was delighted to be confronted with something different for once; the batter here is actually a little sweet, which set off the salty, juicy flavor of the chicken. The taste level was off the charts; if you're a chicken sandwich fan, you're going to want to add this one to your list.

I was halfway through the chicken sandwich when I remembered I still had a burger to eat. It's a super thick patty grilled to perfection, dressed with lettuce and tomato and then topped with a generous pile of grilled onions, Big Poppa sauce and battered-and-fried bacon. Yes, the bacon is battered and fried. I put the whole thing together and dove right in. As soon as I took the first bite, I could tell that this burger was something special- maybe one of the best burgers I've had, and I'm pretty picky when it comes to burgers. It reminded me of the kind of burger you have at backyard family barbecues that just translates into good, old-fashioned comfort food.

I raved about this spot so much that my dad came over and grabbed one of the burgers for himself and LOVED it. If that's not a solid endorsement, I don't know what is. I will definitely be back!

Yum yum yum! I found this place looking for vegan options and I found what I have been searching for!! This place has an entire menu of vegetarian and vegan options... an entire menu!!! My husband and I started with an appetizer of tempura veggies, they were perfectly cooked, had a delicious sauce and came with an assortment of different vegetables. I loved the carrots and the onions, my husband really liked the broccoli. We ordered three different rolls to start, the veggiewoman, the veggie godzilla, and the veggie dragon roll... they were all so delicious. And huge! We could not finish the dragon roll, (that was my husbands favorite of the 3). The Godzilla roll was deep fried and crispy on the outside and so good with the avocado on top! The only thing that made me sad is that I couldn't eat more! The woman who took our order also made our rolls and she was lovely. We stayed for awhile after we finished just talking with her about different things in Reno. This place has two regular customers for sure! We left so full and yet didn't feel gross or heavy, just satisfied happy tummies and good energy. This place is a gem! If you're vegan and haven't tried this place, go now! They have regular sushi too, and also have high chairs for the littles so you can bring the family down, or just come for date night. This will definitely be a new weekly place for us! Yum yum yum! 

We have been back to sushi lover 4 or 5 times since I wrote the first review. The people who work here are amazing, so helpful, friendly and intelligent! Today we sat and talked with them for over an hour after we finished our rolls, the only reason we didn't stay longer was because we had an appointment! I really enjoy learning about their culture and their background, they treat us like we are family and that means a lot! For the people who say they are rude or unhelpful, I don't know what to say! Each time we have been here they have been so accommodating to us! If you're a vegan or vegetarian you will love their selection of rolls, each one is unique. I can't comment on the regular sushi since we go for the veggie menu but give this place a try, relax and you may learn something new! We love this place!

Worst place on the planet! I ordered a cheeseburger and my wife ordered a BBQ chicken pizza.
We waited 15 minutes and they served her small pizza. Mostly dough with an overload of BBQ sauce that tasted straight out of a McDonalds packet. 
As far as my food... well I waited another 15 minutes and no food. So, I finally went up to the cashier (who has his tip jar next to him) and asked about my side of our order. He said "oh it should be right out" another order then two more behind us come out. I go up there again and ask and he says "it's right on it's way".
My food arrived 30 minutes after my wife was served. It was a burger the size of a silver dollar (about 2" wide) and overlooked of course because of the size and cold. I was surprised and passed off by then.
I took it right back to the cashier and said "are you kidding? Look at the size of this burger." He replied "oh, there are two of them stacked on one another" then proceeded to take another walk up order.
What kind of restaurant as they call themselves serves one plate 30 minutes before the  other and doesn't offer to satisfy the customer???!! We could have went to Burger King for a better burger and saves the $18.00.
Do not waste your time eating here. It's a ripoff to say the least!

The last time I visited Australia and New Zealand, my fashionable Sydney cousins (Newtown, darling!) and in fact, pretty much everyone I knew there, were drinking flat whites. It impressed on me that this was The Standard espresso drink for Australia and New Zealand. 

Over here, Recipes Bakery is the only shop in town that serves it. A flat white is similar to a cappuccino, but instead of a dry foam portion, more microfoam is used, resulting in a smooth velvety texture to the drink, and overall has a sweeter flavor without needing sweetener. 
They also serve the long black, which is similar to americano, except that the espresso is added to hot water after, not the other way around, which preserves the crema. 

If you're an Aussie tourist or expat, or simply wishing for a flat white, this is the place to go. They have it down. I once took some some Aussie guests to this town's most artisinal roasting cafe and we just got blank stares when ordering a flat white. 

Their baked goods are made with organic ingredients, I got the cinnamon roll, still warm with icing. If they want to take the Aussie theme a bit farther and start making Anzac biscuits, I will not protest at all!

Recipes Bakery is a shop, not a sit-down cafe, which is too bad, but that's how they are permitted. So everything is packaged "to go."  

One more thing: the whole shop is hyper cutsie. There's a force-field surrounding the place that will separate you from at least half your testosterone upon entering. Much to my surprise I saw one guy in there when I visited. He was sitting in a corner, looking confused, miserable and a little resigned. This is what you'll have to accept for a flat white.

It's just across the street from the Saturday morning farmers market, which is also when they are most busy. Look for the bright pink and white-trimmed cottage.

My first visit to the new Walden's on Wells. I arrived at 10:30 am and the place was totally empty. I had the place to myself the entire time - shame because it's a large space with good food, coffee, and excellent wifi. 

I ordered the carne and eggs, selected bacon for the meat, sourdough toast and fruit instead of potatoes. Cost was $12.99 - a little higher than I expected. The food was indeed good, especially the toast. They told me the sourdough comes from local supplier Franko and it is excellent. Service was friendly and my food delivered quickly. 

Another solid choice for breakfast in Reno. Not sure I'd drive all the way over to Wells often for breakfast, but if you are in the area and need a solid spot I recommend this one. The Walden's coffee is also good but just up the street is Magpie coffee and their lattes are hard to beat.

I wish I lived closer to Burger Me. No, on second thought I'd eat there way too often! Hands down the best burger in Reno/Truckee. My recommendation: Burger with cheddar, grilled onions, avocado, and all the fixings. Just try to say no to that.

Its a casual dining place, walk up to the counter and place your order then find an open table. If they aren't too busy you might get your food delivered to the table, otherwise you have to go get it. If you're in a hurry there is a drive through, but this is not McDonald's. Don't expect the food to be ready by the time you get to the window, someone is actually cooking that burger for you. 

They've got a lot of cool options if you aren't looking for a burger. The Philly Cheese Steak is amazing. There's a bison burger, a stuffed burger, gluten free buns, milkshakes, and beer on tap. What more could you want?

This place has had the harm done to it of being the location of one of my worst dates.  I'll try to detach myself of the displeasure and evaluate Cheese Burger in Paradise on its own merits.  But, should there be some unexpected malice, that's why.

Upon entering, the first thing I noticed was a man in the corner playing a guitar and singing.  It was a Friday night, so I can't imagine there's always a man in the corner playing a guitar, but I can certainly hope there is.  Next to my attention was the pleasantly artificial, tropical ambiance--exactly like stepping into a restaurant in the tropical tourist spots.  The waitstaff was outstanding.  They seemed to sense when their presence was desired and were there bearing menus, refills, or directions to the restroom.  Similarly, the food was fantastic, albeit poorly named--navigating their menu is a chore.  It didn't reheat well though.  Them's the breaks.

The price was a little steep (especially when paying for two), but then, I might simply be projecting my unpleasant time into the cost.  Intellectually speaking, it's actually quite reasonable for such a cute restaurant.  Just be sure you're in the mood for burgers.
Poorly managed and extremely overpriced apartments. Perhaps if they spent some time and money updating the apartments rather than just the lobby this would be a moderately acceptable place to live.

We came here because of all the good reviews but unfortunately we weren't that impressed. We ordered Mediterranean pies Falafel and the Combo (shawarma chicken & beef). The falafel and the combo looked really good (great presentation) but the Mediterranean pies were just taken out of a package a placed in the microwave even though they advertise as authentic Lebanese food? And the falafel was dry and very salty. The combo was just ok. Definitely won't be returning again.


Update-November 2014
After my initial review the owner sent me a message apologizing for our experience and asked us to come back to give them another chance as they want to make sure all customers leave happy. 

Upon arrival he asked us what we didn't like about the food and explained that they do have off days and wanted to make up for it. This time we tried the Shish Kafta and the Roasto Panini and they were both delicious! I'm sure he make an extra effort to make sure it was done well which is fine by me. The lamb was mouth watering and cooked just right. 

We initially gave it 2 out of 5 but now changed to 4 out of 5. I'm glad they reached out otherwise we would have never gone back and had the chance to see why they've had such good reviews. Thanks Romeo.

Really tasty and quality experience! 

It's very spacious and open outside, with more seating inside too. They have really neat vegetarian options that taste like meat, and the famous birria tacos as well.

I had birria tacos for the first time here and even though there are only two, it's very filling and rich. The guac and chips were delicious too, but kinda pricey for a small portion. It was still enough for five of us to share and have a decent amount though.

Service was great, and the ambiance was excellent overall - modest but quality (at least for the outdoors where we ate). 

Would definitely come again to try some of their vegetarian taco/burrito too!

Bishop's Collar is the perfect example of a neighborhood bar done right. Good beer, good grub, good service, good times.

My husband and I went there on Saturday night for a low key dinner out. The draft list was deep but there were two IPAs calling our name, which made for an easy quick choice. We got the Troegs Perpetual IPA and the Green Flash West Coast IPA. $6 isn't too shabby for a high ABV, tasty beer.

For appetizers, we each started with a soup. I went for the creamy corn chowder and my husband went for the beef stew. Both were great in different ways. Mine was creamy with fresh pieces of corn. I tasted the beef stew and it was awesome.  I probably liked it a bit better than the corn chowder. The broth was rich and the  beef was tender. I sampled a few veggies which were soaked in flavor and perfectly cooked. For our mains, I went with the Italian Roast Pork and my husband went with the hot roast beer. The roast pork was so juicy that juices were in fact present. The hot peppers were on the side and I was able to load up my entire sandwich the way I wanted. The only thing missing (and not on the menu) was garlic broccoli rabe. My husband also enjoyed his hot roast beef. I had a bite and it was filled with all the au jus flavor one could ask for. Bishop's Collar isn't where you go for gourmet food, but you are going to get top notch bar food.

I also want to give a shout out to the sides. With any sandwich you get your choice of fries or salad. I appreciate they give you this option up front, without any sort of up-charge. The salad itself is actual greens aka something with actual nutrients. There aren't any toppings but its just a nice serving of mixed greens. Thanks for avoiding iceberg and croutons! 

Til the next time Bishop's Collar.

I really like this place. It's classy, intimate, romantic. I adore the rustic decor and have to fight the urge to stuff one of those tree-trunk lamps in my purse on the way out.

The food is really good, but there aren't really a ton of options for real I-need-to-get-full dinner eating. The stars of the show are the drinks and the cheese plates/charcuterie. There's a whole Google-engineeresque algorithm for choosing the components of your cheese or meat plate. They take that shizz seriously, yo. But the beer and wine lists are crazeamaze (did I just say that?). 

Really lovely. Grab an attractive person and take them here. Everything is sexy over candlelight, braised pork belly, wine I can't pronounce, and tree-trunk lamps.

The BEST. Vietnamese restaurant. In town.

The food is amazing. Wish they made a dish differently?  Ask. They will. Diane who owns the place is CONSTANTLY there, always checking in with her customers to make SURE EVERYTHING is PERFECT. My wife and I had NO idea where to start when we first showed up there and the waiter played 20 questions with us to see what we liked and just brought us dishes. They were... PERFECT. I wanted extra noodles. They gave me a double batch... no extra charge!!! I liked the fish sauce a lot... they brought out an extra dish of it. Free. The service is ALWAYS amazing, SO polite, SO attentive... The food is ALWAYS top notch and VERY competitively priced. The atmosphere is even comfortable... my wife and I love to laugh about the music, because it's usually very "Vietnamesey" covers of classic mainstream American soft rock hits. You haven't lived until you've heard Mambo Italiano performed solo on a Casio Keyboard in bossa nova time. EPIC. Did I mention the food comes out in a timely fashion 99% of the time, AND they DELIVER??? I've been to literally 8 other viet places in STL, and now that I've been to Dao Tien, I only get mad at myself when I bother with anyone else. There's just NO. POINT. GO to Dao Tien... or just accept that you're not a fan of good food, good service, and good prices.

After living on Main Street for over 10 years, there is finally a dIner that I can walk to.  The space is in a two-story converted row home, newly renovated with a cozy style, right in the heart of the Manayunk.

I was greeted as soon as I walked in and was seated at a 5 chair coffee bar. Service was attentive and breakfast took about the right amount of time as everything is cooked to order.

I ordered the standard, 2 eggs SSU, bacon, home fries, and toast.  Eggs and bacon were perfect, home fries (added onions) we exceptional.

Looking forward to trying the benedicts and the lunch options.

It would be rally nice to see Diner@Manaunk stick around.

I absolutely LOVE Red Perch! It's so nice to have a great food spot down the street from my office. 

The owners are extremely responsive on social media. I inquired about gluten free options and was told they have a dedicated fryer for their fries AND they can grill the fish instead of fry it.

Later on, I found out they went out and bought gluten free soy sauce just so I could have the poke! Seriously, above and beyond customer service.

This restaurant has a lot going for it, although extensive hours are not among them. Come during the seating times (1130, 1145, 1200, 530, 600) and be the test audience for students at the Art Institute's culinary school. 

It succeeds at it's goal - to be a 4-star dining experience with admittedly student staff. It's clear that they've been trained and are striving for that level of service and quality, though as students there are still a few rough edges you wouldn't see at a really fancy place. Give them another few months and they'll be great. And that's exactly why instead of paying $40 for lunch, you only pay a $15 prix fixe for a 4-course meal, including drinks!

While most dishes were good, the strong standouts for us were the spicy scallop amuse bouche and the excellent soups - potato-leek, shrimp wonton, and lentil. The chocolate truffle in the final course far outpaced all the other desserts.

We gave them 3 times to get it right. Overpriced breakfast. The kitchen is always "behind" and never gets out orders right. They also have you wait for your food so long when it does come out it is cold and over done. 
So many other mom and pop diners for a much better experience.
This is my first time here! Very good service! Food was great!! Specially the Oysters Poboy. I will come back! Average per person $30 range!

Xmas eve reservation.  Empty restaurant but was asked to wait 10 minutes for a 615p reservation because I was 10 minutes early.  $7 valet.  No signs until we left (valet told us) that it was a charge.  Tip not included.  Food was ok for a mid-tier restaurant but prices are extremely overpriced.  I've eaten numerous times at competing steakhouses in Nashville and this so much more expensive for the value.  $20 "kid" plates (bowl of spiral noodles).  We ordered a vegan dish of a (small) cauliflower steak on a (small) bed of risotto...$35/each!!!  Sticker shock.  I asked for the house white wine and was given an $18 glass.  Not the house.  Bottom line, if you want a top m-tier steakhouse in Nashville, go to Michael Mina's restaurant at JW Marriott.  I won't be back.

Dingy and run down. My first time having German food so wasn't sure what to expect. The fried pickle appetizer was so delicious. Ended up getting the spicy sausage plate with red and white cabbage. The sausage was NOT spicy AT ALL and lacked flavor. The red cabbage was really good. Went with a party of 6 and sat at a table, the chairs are so old and wobbly I felt like it was going to break and I was going to fall!

Very cheap and rude.  Used to love coming to this place, and the food is good, but tried to redeem 8 receipts and they acted like I was trying to rip them off.

Treated me like crap and embarrassed a good customer in front of the store.

Many times they overcharged me and I didn't even mention it, because I didn't want to insult them.

Never going there again.  The food is good though.
